extracted.intended_audience: book and book-cover designers, design studios, publishers, and entrants to the AIGA 50 Books | 50 Covers competition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for submitting and having book and book-cover design entries judged in the AIGA 50 Books | 50 Covers juried competition. Covers expectations about design qualities, juried selection, and submission logistics (deadlines, fees, recognition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-designed books and book covers
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition identifies the 50 best-designed books and book covers of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a time-honored survey (originating in 1923) that recognizes the best of book and book cover design from around the world; winners are published in the Winners Gallery and preserved in design archives (AIGA Design Archives, Denver Art Museum, RBML at Columbia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful and compelling book design
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should demonstrate powerful and compelling book design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language on the page emphasizes 'powerful and compelling' as the core quality being celebrated; the competition looks for work that stands out and resonates visually and conceptually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design that engages readers and encourages turning the page
rubrics_metrics.description: Design should have the 'timeless, magnetic power' to engage readers and encourage them to turn the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explicitly frames engagement—how a book invites reading—as an evaluative quality. Judges value design that shapes reader behavior and curiosity, not merely ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / pushing the discipline further
rubrics_metrics.description: Design that demonstrates new ways of working with publishers and printers and pushes the discipline of book design forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juror commentary notes it was encouraging to see designers 'developing new ways of working with publishers and printers to push our discipline further.' Innovation in process, collaboration, and technique is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic and image relationships (placement, position, scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to the relationship between typography and images, including placement, position, and scale, is a judged quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted juror observation: 'The exciting part about opening any new book... is the power it has to influence your relationship to typography or images—by its placement, position or scale.' Judges look for thoughtful interplay between type and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic qualities: bold typography, texture, and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Stylistic attributes such as bold typography, tactile texture, and wit are noted characteristics of award-winning designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site references winner-explanations (e.g., 2018 winners) where designers cite 'bold typography, texture, and a ton of wit'—these are concrete stylistic signals the jurors have rewarded in past years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material qualities and production values
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the book's material qualities and production (paper, printing, binding, tactile decisions) as part of design excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentions of 'material qualities of communication' and physical archiving of winners imply that production choices and materiality are part of what the competition recognizes; jurors and winning designers often reference printers and production as part of innovation and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative, context, and cultural sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Design that responds to narrative, context, and culture—treating the book as a portable exhibition and lasting cultural record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alberto Rigau's practice focuses on 'narratives, context, and culture' and treats 'each book as a portable exhibition and lasting cultural record,' indicating judges value design that meaningfully engages subject matter and cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design systems and custom typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of coherent design systems and custom typography in book and editorial design is a positive criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scott Vander Zee's expertise and juror bio emphasize 'design systems, and custom typography,' signaling that systematic design thinking and typographic craft are criteria for excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic thinking and long-term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Design grounded in strategic thinking with an emphasis on long-term impact is valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lauren Vajda's description highlights work 'grounded in strategic thinking and long-term impact,' suggesting judges consider strategy and the enduring relevance of a design beyond immediate novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry logistics: deadlines, fees, and membership discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must meet stated deadlines and fee schedules (early discount, regular, final, late), with different pricing for AIGA members and non-members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are specific and time-zone-bound (all deadlines 11:59 p.m. ET). Fee schedule for 2026 example: Early (Jan 12) AIGA members $75 / non-members $110; Regular (Mar 16) members $100 / non-members $135; Final (Apr 13) members $150 / non-members $185; Late (Apr 27) members $165 / non-members $200. Joining AIGA reduces entry cost. Notifications of selection are emailed in summer and winners are showcased publicly.
